This allows FortiGate to correctly match incoming IKEv2 initiations with the appropriate tunnel.If the Network ID is not defined, FortiGate cannot reliably determine which Phase 1 configuration to use when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels reside on the same interface. This behavior differs from IKEv1, where Peer IDs were used to distinguish between tunnels. Use the following CLI syntax to define the Network ID for each Phase 1 configuration: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ike-version 2 set network-overlay enable set network-id next end The Network ID must be defined on both the FortiGate Phase1 and the FortiClient configuration to ensure correct tunnel matching.Note: The Network ID setting cannot be configured on unmanaged or standalone Forticlient. incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error "New image is too big"
incidents.solution: Typically, this error occurs during a firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image.This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: "New image is too big”.This is Bug ID 1329518 in the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Known Issues.Most common causes:Insufficient flash disk space – The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process.Small virtual disk allocation – The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps:Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example.Check flash disk usage:Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status:ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) Use% BootImage RunningImage primary FLVM64-8.0-FW-build0105-2

incidents.title: 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: Description This articles describes an issue where the 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 Scope FortiGate 1800F, FortiGate 1801F, FortiOS 7.6.8 Solution Following an internal driver update introduced in FortiOS 7.6.8, the affected platforms - FortiGate 1800F and 1801F is unable to process traffic over its GE SFP slots. As a summary:GE SFP ports 17-24 are unable to process traffic.Traffic through SFP ports 25-40 is unaffected.Traffic through GE RJ45 ports is unaffected.
